Impact

Breaking the Policy Silos

The Problem
Governments often operate in silos. For example, before our training & workshops on Aligning Goals, officials from Suriname and Somalia identified "limited coordination" and a lack of "awareness/alignment" between leading institutions as a primary barrier to a realistic national strategy.
The Outcome after our intervention
  • 100% Coordination breakthrough: Every participant surveyed reported that the course helped them identify new, specific points for inter-agency coordination within their government.
  • Understanding of the intersection of petroleum, national development goals, and NDCs shifted from a baseline of "Some" to "High" or "Very High".
  • Participants gave a nearly perfect score when asked if the learning would directly impact their work performance, indicating a high level of practical utility.
Impact

Suriname – Asserting its Carbon-Negative Status

The Challenge
Suriname, a carbon-negative nation, faces the complex task of developing significant offshore oil discoveries without compromising its global environmental leadership.
The Intervention
In 2023 NP4SE provided a strategic White Paper and technical briefings to the Surinamese government, outlining how new producers can aim for the lowest sector emissions while investing in carbon negative projects that support national development goals.
The Impact
At COP28, President Chan Santokhi utilized NP4SE’s research to declare a clear national mandate: “Suriname will maintain its carbon negative status even when the offshore oil and gas industry is developed.” This demonstrated how the network equips heads of state with the technical confidence to navigate global climate politics.

Resources

  • Annual Meeting 2024

    The context had changed significantly in Suriname since the 2017 meeting, thanks to nine offshore discoveries in the last six years. However, Suriname is not yet a producer and, when it is, the country intends to remain carbon neutral. The Annual meeting included a two-day international roundtable on 3-4 June focused on the incentives and obstacles involved in developing natural gas and managing greenhouse gas emissions, followed by interactive training sessions on ‘Contracts and fiscal systems in the transition’ and ‘Emissions management’ on 5 June.

  • three working groups

    The 5th annual meeting of the New Producers Group was hosted by Staatsolie in Suriname. The international group meeting focused on creating investment terms that incentivize oil companies to perform financially and operationally to the highest standards as well as contract administration and operational oversight issues. At the meeting, the group established, which aim to produce practical toolkits helping policymakers and regulators in the oversight of oil and gas operations. The meeting included training sessions on assessing environmental impacts, understanding the effect of evolving global climate policy on petroleum projects, establishing a fit-for-purpose NOC, and ensuring effective project oversight.
